name: Captions and subtitles
observations: OpenMontage's CaptionOverlay accepts word-level records with word, startMs, endMs, and optional pageBreakAfter fields; defaults are 6 words per page, 42px text, cyan active-word highlight, translucent dark background, and a space separator (remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:11-39,165-175).

Pages are constructed in input order, flushed when wordsPerPage is reached or pageBreakAfter is true, and assigned startMs from the first word and endMs from the last word (remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:56-80).

For each page, the visible Remotion Sequence starts at Math.round(page.startMs / 1000 * fps); its duration extends to the next page start, or 500ms after the current page end for the final page, with a minimum duration of one frame (remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:176-193).

Within a page, current time is computed as page.startMs + frame/fps*1000. A word is active for startMs <= currentMs < endMs, past when endMs <= currentMs, and otherwise receives a dimmed color (remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:91-96,134-151).

Each page enters with a Remotion spring using damping 18 and stiffness 120, then translates from 20px below to its resting position; CSS transitions are explicitly disabled (remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:97-102,116-117,146-147).

The page wrapper is bottom-aligned with 80px bottom padding, centered, max-width 80%, and text centered. Words are inline-block and nowrap; the supplied wordSeparator is rendered between words (remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:104-155).

Direction supports ltr, rtl, and auto. Auto counts words containing Hebrew/Arabic/Persian/Urdu-range characters versus Latin/Greek/Cyrillic-range characters and selects RTL only when the RTL count is greater (remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:41-54,165-180). The wrapper sets both dir and CSS direction (lines 112-115).

TalkingHead renders captions as the topmost layer above video and other overlays and forwards wordsPerPage, fontSize, highlightColor, caption colors, optional font family, and optional separator (remotion-composer/src/TalkingHead.tsx:298-311,313-363).

The composer declares @remotion/captions ^4.0.484 in both package.json and package-lock.json, but CaptionOverlay has no import from that package and repository searches found no @remotion/captions call site in the relevant composer/tools/tests (remotion-composer/package.json:10-23; remotion-composer/package-lock.json:7-23).

The Remotion burn tool converts word-level transcript timestamps to integer millisecond WordCaption records, supports segment words or proportional timing from segment text, optionally parses SRT into per-word timing, writes props under the Remotion public directory, probes source duration and dimensions, and renders TalkingHead at source dimensions with fixed 30fps (tools/video/remotion_caption_burn.py:184-263,269-341).

The Remotion burn path is preferred when npx and an installed composer are available; otherwise FFmpeg burns temporary SRT cues in groups of four words. The fallback uses fixed styling and does not implement animated active-word highlighting (tools/video/remotion_caption_burn.py:364-443,449-494).

SubtitleGen independently emits SRT, VTT, or caption JSON; it groups word records by maximum words and characters, supports none/word_by_word/karaoke output modes, applies case-insensitive corrections while preserving punctuation, and formats timestamps by rounding total milliseconds before decomposition so carries cross second/minute/hour boundaries (tools/subtitle/subtitle_gen.py:26-40,82-129,131-227,229-335).

The target has focused regression/source-contract tests for RTL direction, Remotion props path handling, timestamp carry correctness, and workspace isolation. The environment lacked the pytest executable, so those tests were not run here (tests/contracts/test_caption_rtl_direction_contract.py:1-49; tests/tools/test_remotion_caption_burn.py:1-56; tests/tools/test_subtitle_timestamps.py:1-50).
The target repository contains a top-level LICENSE file; this analysis treats the requested target license as AGPL-3.0 and did not copy source, assets, or implementation text.
inferences: Caption timing is frame-quantized twice: page activation is rounded to a frame boundary, while active-word comparisons use the frame-derived millisecond clock. Therefore sub-frame timestamp differences cannot be represented exactly and boundary behavior is determined by fps rounding.

A page remains mounted until the next page starts rather than until its own final word ends, so any gap between pages is covered by the preceding page and the final page receives a 500ms hold after its last word.
Because all pages are rendered in separate Sequences and PageRenderer computes frame from its local Sequence, spring entrance restarts for every page and currentMs restarts from that page's startMs.
The `pageBreakAfter` field is a presentation grouping control, not a source subtitle cue boundary; it changes page partitioning but does not alter word timestamps.

The declared @remotion/captions dependency appears preparatory or unused in this subsystem; current behavior is custom React/Remotion rendering rather than the package's caption parsing/rendering APIs.
The FFmpeg fallback is only approximate parity with the Remotion path: it uses four-word groups, fixed bottom styling, and no RTL/CJK-specific separator or direction propagation.
OpenMontage has two distinct caption products: burned-in animated word captions for the Remotion talking-head composition and standalone timed subtitle/caption files from SubtitleGen.

MPS's current MPVE renderer can produce a valid silent MP4, but it has no evidence of a synchronized caption artifact or caption burn stage in the local provider; adding captions would require an explicit provider integration rather than a small component-level change.
unknowns: No runtime render was performed, so actual visual wrapping, font availability, spring appearance, bidi layout, and behavior with empty, malformed, overlapping, or out-of-order words remain unverified.
No direct @remotion/captions API usage exists in the inspected relevant source, so the intended reason for retaining that dependency and any planned parser integration are unknown.
The available tests were not executed because pytest is not installed in the environment; source-contract assertions were inspected only.

It is not established whether consumers rely on the default 30fps in the burn tool versus the composition's configured fps, or whether source videos with variable frame rate create synchronization drift.
It is not established whether MPS hosts can supply word-level timestamps, SRT/VTT, caption style settings, locale/direction, or a caption provider through an undocumented integration.
No evidence was found that MPS's current static SVG fallback or local Pillow renderer emits timed subtitle sidecar files or burns captions into frames.
contracts: Input contract: caption words carry text plus millisecond start/end times; optional pageBreakAfter forces a page flush. Caller controls page size and visual styling through CaptionOverlay props (remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:11-39,62-79,165-180).

Timing contract: page sequence start is round(startMs*fps/1000); non-final page duration is round((nextPage.startMs-page.startMs)*fps/1000), final duration is round((page.endMs+500-page.startMs)*fps/1000), clamped to at least one frame (remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:181-203).

Highlight contract: active means start inclusive/end exclusive; future words are rendered as base color plus an appended 99 alpha suffix, past words use base color, and active words use highlightColor (remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:134-151).

Rendering contract: caption overlay is topmost in TalkingHead, bottom-centered, and must not use CSS transitions because Remotion rendering is frame-driven (remotion-composer/src/TalkingHead.tsx:328-363; remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:104-123,146-147).

Localization contract: callers may select explicit ltr/rtl or auto majority detection; CJK callers can pass an empty word separator; each word is kept unbroken with inline-block/nowrap (remotion-composer/src/components/CaptionOverlay.tsx:30-38,112-155).

Burn-tool contract: input requires input_path and output_path plus either segments or srt_path; Remotion is preferred when available, with FFmpeg fallback; output existence is treated as success evidence (tools/video/remotion_caption_burn.py:76-143,449-494).

Standalone subtitle contract: SubtitleGen accepts transcript segments and outputs SRT, VTT, or JSON, with configurable cue word/character limits and highlight style (tools/subtitle/subtitle_gen.py:42-72,82-129).

MPS contract: MPVE result exposes artifact/provider/duration/aspect/audio/fallback/errors/quality gates, and failed or fallback-only output must not be treated as mastery; current docs explicitly say synchronized captions remain host/provider extensions (MPS-git/docs/mpve-api.md:37-56; MPS-git/docs/mpve-report.md:60-67).
mps_gaps: MPS has no corresponding CaptionOverlay/React composition and no @remotion/captions dependency or usage in the inspected repository.

MPS's local cinematic renderer draws narration text into scene frames as static visual content but does not consume word-level timings or produce synchronized active-word captions (MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:143-180).
MPS's RenderResult has an audio boolean but no caption/subtitle artifact, caption timing payload, locale/direction, style, or burn method (MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:35-56).

MPS's provider flow reports local-cinematic as silent and hosted-provider as audio-capable by assumption, but neither path exposes a synchronized caption contract; the docs classify captions as a future host/provider extension (MPS-git/docs/mpve-report.md:58-67).
MPS's MPVE request/result API has no documented captions, subtitles, transcript, language, or caption-style fields (MPS-git/docs/mpve-api.md:9-56).
MPS has no evident equivalent to OpenMontage's Remotion-to-FFmpeg fallback that preserves a common word-caption input while selecting animated or static burn paths.
MPS has no tested equivalent for RTL majority detection, explicit dir/CSS direction, CJK separators, page breaks, active-word boundaries, or millisecond carry-safe SRT/VTT formatting.
clean_room_recommendations: Define an independently authored caption boundary in MPVE with a neutral timed-word schema such as word plus start/end milliseconds, optional cue/page grouping, locale/direction, and style; keep it separate from MPS pedagogy and mastery state.

Expose captions as optional request configuration and result metadata, preserving MPS's current valid-silent behavior when no caption provider is configured. Report caption status, sidecar paths, and burn method explicitly rather than implying synchronization.

Implement a deterministic frame-based renderer or post-process that specifies rounding, inclusive/exclusive word boundaries, page hold behavior, empty-input behavior, and final-frame handling; add tests around exact frame boundaries and timestamp carry across seconds/minutes/hours.

Provide two independently implemented output modes: timed SRT/VTT/JSON sidecars and burned-in captions. If a provider is unavailable, make fallback behavior explicit and avoid claiming animated karaoke parity when only static subtitles are burned.

Include localization requirements from the outset: explicit RTL direction support, majority-based auto detection only as a convenience, CJK no-separator configuration, and tests for mixed-script and punctuation cases.

Add provider capability negotiation for word-level alignment versus segment-level timing, and define proportional fallback timing when only segment start/end is available; surface reduced precision in the manifest.

Add MPVE integration tests that submit a caption-enabled request, verify caption metadata in the result, inspect sidecar validity, and confirm the written explanation/mastery flow remains owned by MPS.

Do not port OpenMontage implementation text or assets; use only the independently stated behavioral contracts above and validate any new implementation against public format specifications and MPS-owned tests.
